topicName: Azure Firewall, Bastion, and Private Endpoints/Links
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Enterprise Azure Networking: Securing Workloads with Firewall, Bastion, and Private Endpoints"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Designing a secure cloud architecture in Microsoft Azure requires a defense-in-depth approach. Public IP exposures should be minimized, inbound traffic must be thoroughly inspected, and outbound traffic needs strict governance. This technical tutorial explores how to integrate Azure Firewall, Azure Bastion, and Azure Private Endpoints to build a highly secure, enterprise-grade hub-and-spoke network."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Architectural Overview"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Hub Virtual Network: Houses shared services, Azure Firewall, and Azure Bastion."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Spoke Virtual Networks: Contain application workloads connected via VNet Peering."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Azure Firewall: Controls inbound, outbound, and east-west traffic using Network and Application rules."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Azure Bastion: Provides secure, seamless RDP and SSH connectivity to virtual machines over SSL without public IPs on the VMs."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Private Endpoints: Enable secure access to Azure PaaS services (such as Azure SQL or Storage) entirely within the Microsoft backbone network."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 1: Deploying Azure Firewall in the Hub VNet"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Azure Firewall must be deployed in a dedicated subnet named 'AzureFirewallSubnet'. Below is an Azure CLI script to create the hub network, firewall subnet, and the firewall itself."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"az network vnet create --resource-group rg-hub-net --name vnet-hub --address-prefix 10.0.0.0/16 --subnet-name AzureFirewallSubnet --subnet-prefix 10.0.1.0/24
az azfw create --name fw-hub --resource-group rg-hub-net --location eastus --vnet-name vnet-hub"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 2: Configuring Azure Bastion for Secure Management"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"To allow administrators to connect to spoke VMs without assigning public IP addresses to the virtual machines, provision Azure Bastion in a subnet named 'AzureBastionSubnet'."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"az network vnet subnet create --resource-group rg-hub-net --vnet-name vnet-hub --name AzureBastionSubnet --address-prefix 10.0.2.0/26
az network public-ip create --resource-group rg-hub-net --name pip-bastion --sku Standard --allocation-method Static
az network bastion create --name bastion-hub --resource-group rg-hub-net --public-ip-address pip-bastion --vnet-name vnet-hub --location eastus"},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 3: Implementing Private Endpoints for PaaS Services"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"Private Endpoints eliminate data exfiltration risks by injecting a private IP from your virtual network into your PaaS resources. Create a private endpoint for an Azure Storage Account using the CLI."},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"az network private-endpoint create \
  --resource-group rg-spoke-net \
  --name pe-storage-blob \
  --vnet-name vnet-spoke \
  --subnet subnet-workload \
  --private-connection-resource-id /subscriptions/{sub-id}/resourceGroups/rg-storage/providers/Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/mystorageacct \
  --group-id blob \
  --connection-name conn-storage-blob"},{"order":18,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 4: Integrating DNS with Private Endpoints"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"For Private Endpoints to resolve correctly, you must configure private DNS zones. Link the Private DNS Zone 'privatelink.blob.core.windows.net' to your hub and spoke virtual networks."},{"order":20,"type":"code","text":"az network private-dns zone create --resource-group rg-hub-net --name privatelink.blob.core.windows.net
az network private-dns link vnet create --resource-group rg-hub-net --zone-name privatelink.blob.core.windows.net --name dns-link-hub --virtual-network vnet-hub --registration-enabled false"},{"order":21,"type":"subheading","text":"Validation and Best Practices"},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Route Tables (UDR): Ensure spoke subnets have a route table forcing 0.0.0.0/0 traffic to the Azure Firewall private IP."},{"order":23,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Network Security Groups (NSGs): Apply NSGs to subnets as a micro-segmentation layer, complementing the centralized Azure Firewall rules."},{"order":24,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Monitoring: Enable Azure Firewall Diagnostic Logs and route them to a Log Analytics workspace for threat intelligence and auditing."}]
